_comment: FIXTURE PATTERNS for tools/test.sh, not a profile. Same schema as profile.example/gitops-substitutions.json (docs/gitops-substitutions-schema.md). Paths are relative to --repo, which the test points at a temp copy of fixtures/gitops/, so the generated overlay never lands in the source tree.
_exclude_comment: One live exclusion (the data-plane component) and one deliberately stale entry. The stale one is the point: a pinned exclusion that no longer matches a real component must be reported, never swallowed.
_auto_comment: The last two pairs are the longest-first exhibit, and their file order is deliberately the WRONG one: the general CIDR prefix also matches the hub subnet, so applying these in the order written would rewrite the subnet with the general mapping and the specific rule would then find nothing. Only the length sort produces the expected output — which is what makes the assertion able to fail.

auto.why: hub subnet, re-planned in DR rather than swapped straight across

post_apply.what: the DR ingress identity resource id
post_apply.why: the id carries the source name prefix, so a token-by-token rewrite yields a plausible id that points at nothing

post_apply.what: the DR ingress workload identity client id
post_apply.why: DR identities are new, with new client ids that do not exist until the identity root applies

decide.what: on-prem source ranges trusted by the internal gateway
decide.why: on-prem reaches DR over the same links, so keeping the source list is usually right — but confirm it

decide.what: the DNS zone the cluster's DNS controller writes into
decide.why: keeping the source zone would have the DR cluster write live production records

_forbidden_residual_comment: The completeness guard. The cutover hostname is deliberately absent: it legitimately survives into the DR overlay.

forbidden_residual.why: source resource name prefix survived the rewrite
source region token survived the rewrite
